perennials/7bc1b39:
The inversion the sun work was building toward: the yard's computed site
conditions flow into the browse query instead of only being read off it.
Bed lines gain an Open in the guide action that navigates to the browse
page with the bed's derived light word applied as an ordinary Light
constraint, and a new Ask tool on the sheet reads the sun at any tapped
point — hours of direct light for the scrubbed season, in the
catalogue's own spelling — with the same two actions a bed gets: open
the guide on it, or save it as a spot named by the nearest label.

The derived word is an ask, never a claim about a plant, so no lane is
crossed; the answer prints its basis (her latitude, her span, crowns and
land as recorded) and follows the year scrubber, because the scene
carries the slot's day. Without latitude or span the tool shows the same
two-number form the model's sun section uses — extracted as one shared
fragment — and computes nothing. Her zone deliberately does not ride
along on the guide link: homeZone starts at 6 without her ever saying
so, and a filter is a stronger claim than a sort.

tierWord moves from the page into lib/sun.ts and is pinned by rules:
a derived tier always lands on a value the light facet actually
carries, sceneOf without either of her numbers is null, and an
ask-derived atom survives the URL round trip.
perennials/7ba8735:
Her bloom marks and USDA's period have sat side by side without ever
being compared: she could mark a plant blooming in April against a
printed Late Spring band and the guide kept quiet about it. That
silence wasted the one reading only she can produce, a real date in
the actual yard against a continent average.

lib/phenology.ts holds the comparison, pure: outsideRecord() gives her
slots the printed band does not cover, in the year's order, and
phenologyLine() says the divergence in one sentence, her sighting as
fact and the period as USDA's by name, neither called wrong. Both are
empty unless both records exist. A missing period is a gap in our data,
not a band she can fall outside of, so the line can never turn our own
absence into a claim; and with no marks nothing was witnessed.

The bloom row prints the line under its chips in her sepia, and the
calendar's per-plant word-line switches to it, since the sentence
already names both records the line used to name. The rules are pinned
in rules.test.ts: inside the band claims nothing, outside it names
exactly the out-of-record slots, and either side missing stays silent.
